name: Neck firming band

lead: Neck firming bands are consumer products worn around the neck or under the chin, marketed for a smoother, firmer neckline and a tighter jaw-to-neck transition. People use them to address visible vertical neck bands, loose skin and a soft jawline, concerns often grouped as an ageing neck.

The visible bands are usually linked to the platysma, a thin neck muscle whose tone and shape change with age. For platysma prominence, the best-documented treatment is botulinum toxin; a 2025 phase 3 trial reported improvement versus placebo. No published trial was found testing wearable neck bands themselves.

paras: The band is worn around the neck for a set period, sometimes during sleep or alongside neck exercises, and users report gradual or temporary smoothing. Routines often combine it with skincare and posture work.

Pressure from tight straps may cause skin irritation or marks, and anything compressing the neck should be worn loosely. People with neck, circulation or skin conditions typically check with a clinician first.

angle.text: Users wear the band hoping to hold the neck skin and muscle in a smoother position and sharpen the jaw-neck line. Effects described by users are short-term and tied to wearing the band.

lead: A neck firming band is a wearable strap or elastic band worn around the neck, and sometimes the chin, that people use in the hope of improving the look of neck bands, sagging skin and a soft neck-jaw contour.

The visible vertical bands in an ageing neck are associated with the platysma, a thin superficial muscle. Wikipedia notes that wrinkling and reduced muscle tone can thin and shorten the muscle, and that neck bands become most noticeable with age.[1]

Established treatments for neck bands include botulinum toxin injections and surgical platysmaplasty.[1] A randomized phase 3 trial of onabotulinumtoxinA reported improvement in platysma prominence versus placebo.[2] No published trial has tested wearable neck bands.
infobox: Neck bands, loose neck skin, jawline

paras: The platysma is a thin muscle in the neck; with age it can thin and shorten, and neck bands become more noticeable.[1] Conservative management, botulinum toxin and platysmaplasty are listed treatment options.[1]

No studies found on neck firming bands themselves. In a related randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial of onabotulinumtoxinA for moderate to severe platysma prominence, 32.3 percent of treated participants versus 1.9 percent of placebo participants reached a minimal or mild rating with at least two grades of improvement at day 14, with adverse event rates similar between groups.[2]
